subject: Cloud Computing
title: Kubernetes: Google's Gift to Cloud
description: A fast breakdown of Kubernetes: Google's Gift to Cloud for builders.

hook.text: Google ran billions of containers with a secret system called Borg. In 2014, they shared it.

buildup.text: Kubernetes automates deploying, scaling, and managing containers across many servers.

discovery.text: It became the industry standard. Every major cloud provider now offers managed Kubernetes.

twist.text: Google open-sourced Kubernetes — but benefits most when you run it on Google Cloud.

climax.text: Kubernetes is so dominant that cloud strategy now often means container strategy.

punchline.text: Google gave away Borg's successor. It reshaped cloud computing.

quiz.question: What was the Google internal system that inspired Kubernetes?

details.summary: Google open-sourced Kubernetes in 2014, sharing its internal container orchestration expertise with the world. Kubernetes automates deploying, scaling, and managing containerized applications, becoming the standard platform for running containers in the cloud.
details.whyItMatters: Kubernetes became the de facto standard for container orchestration, supported by every major cloud provider. It created a portable abstraction layer that reduces vendor lock-in.
takeaways: Google open-sourced Kubernetes based on its internal Borg system
It automates deployment, scaling, and management of containers
Every major cloud provider offers managed Kubernetes services

faq.question: Why did Google open-source Kubernetes?
faq.answer: Google trailed AWS in cloud market share. By open-sourcing Kubernetes, Google positioned itself as a cloud-native thought leader and created a portable platform that reduced the advantage of AWS-specific services. It was a strategic move to level the competitive playing field.

faq.question: What problems does Kubernetes solve?
faq.answer: Kubernetes handles container scheduling across clusters, automatic scaling based on demand, self-healing by restarting failed containers, rolling deployments with zero downtime, service discovery, and load balancing for containerized applications.
